postTitle: Fee Optimization: The Silent Drag on Your Returns
topic: The fee on a statement can be one part of what investing costs each year

assumptions.notes: Illustrative €100,000 invested. Layers from the blog's ranges: fund fee 1.0% (blog: 0.5 to 1.5%) = €1,000; platform 0.3% (0.15 to 0.45%) = €300; adviser 1.0% (0.5 to 1.5%) = €1,000; trading inside the fund and tax drag about 0.3% = €300. Total 2.6% = €2,600, inside the blog's 'could easily total 2 to 3%'.

barStory.disclosure: Illustrative. Costs vary by product, company and country.

hookVariants.narration: Your statement shows one yearly fee. Is that everything you pay?
onscreenLines: Your statement shows one yearly fee

beats.narration: On a hundred thousand euros invested, the fee you see is one thousand a year.
The company holding your account charges its own fee.
beats.subtext: Its own fee, on top: about €300

beats.narration: An adviser can add another thousand.
Trading and tax cost money too. These two smaller parts: about three hundred each.
Together: two thousand six hundred euros a year, in this example.
beats.onscreenText: Fees and other costs: €2,600 a year
